<p><b>Autosomal</b> (atDNA) : les 22 pai:
Autosomal (atDNA): the 22 pairs of non-sex chromosomes, received half from each parent. It finds cousins on all sides back to about 5 to 8 generations. It is the most common “genealogy” test.

Y-DNA: passed from father to son almost unchanged. It follows a single line, often the surname line, over hundreds of years. It is studied through its markers (Y-STR: 37, 67, 111 markers…) and its mutations (SNPs), which give the haplogroup.

Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA): passed by the mother to all her children; only daughters pass it on. Very stable: useful for old questions or to tell two maternal lines apart.

X-DNA: its special way of being passed on rules out some ancestors (see “Y, mt and X lines”).
<p>Dans un village isolé, une île, une c: In an isolated village, an island or a closed community, you descend several times from the same ancestors (pedigree collapse). You then share more DNA than expected, in many small segments: relationships look closer than they are. Be wary of the estimates; look at the longest segment.
<p>Le <b>centimorgan</b> mesure une long: The centimorgan measures a “genetic” length of DNA. You share about 3,400 to 3,700 cM with a parent, 850 on average with a first cousin, 230 with a second cousin… The total and the length of the longest segment help guess the relationship (“📐 Calculator”). Small segments (under 7 to 8 cM) are often “noise” or very old.
<p>Mise au point par Dana Leeds : on pre: Devised by Dana Leeds: take the matches from 90 to 400 cM (2nd and 3rd cousins) and colour together those that match each other. You often get 4 groups (your 4 grandparents) or 8 (your great-grandparents). You need to note each one’s “shared matches” (“🗂️ Groups”).
<p>Si A correspond avec toi, B correspon: If A matches you, B matches you, and A and B match each other on the same segment, that segment very probably comes from an ancestor shared by all three. It is the best genetic proof of a branch. The “🧩 chromosome browser” shows the overlaps to check.
<p>Un <b>haplogroupe</b> (R-M269, I-M253: A haplogroup (R-M269, I-M253, H1, U5b…) gathers everyone descended from the same distant ancestor in the Y or mt line, often thousands of years ago. Two people in the same haplogroup are not necessarily close: you need fine subclades or a marker match.
